Who doesn't want more games like those?

Me. They might be successful, and even wildly popular, but so is CoD, and for fuck's sake, we have enough of those. "Critical success," while great for your pocketbook, shouldn't be an argument that stands on its own; though I freely admit that to anyone with a powerful need to eat, it certainly does.

Indie games were prized once for their individuality and ability to do what the AAA titles couldn't: experiment with new ideas and explore new ways of presenting content. These days, once an indie game sees commercial success, there are immediately forty clones of it, and the developer makes a dozen sequels, never bothering to break the mold that formed his/her success. It's tedium, and it will be the doom of the medium (heh).

I get what you're saying, but this article does a disservice to that argument. Not only are they successful games that he uses as an example, but they are great games in my opinion. Not a one of those games listed in the article is a clone of the other in any way other than a vague thematic thread that seems to be shared... innocence in a world of danger and corruption. Besides a few that are similar simply because they are platformers, they each innovate on the genre in their own way and can hardly be accused of cutting corners or making a cash grab on a previous phenomenon without at least adding their own voice.

Just because Limbo spawned an army of clones and copycats does not mean that that game is an affront to creativity in the indie scene. You mentioned these games are coming out with sequel after sequel, but not a single example given in the article even has a sequel (maybe Inside as a spiritual successor to Limbo, or Transistor as a successor to Bastion, but that's all) Furthermore, its only natural that others would try to duplicate the level of success those titles have.

I fail to see where this golden age of indie creativity was before games like Bastion, Limbo, Braid, Never Alone, Transistor, Ico (does that even count as an indie title?), Ori and the Blind Forest, Journey, Fez and many, many more titles.Yet people always seem to shit on these games. And the worst part is, these games only occupy a small part of the market and if anything bring more gamers into the fold with their attractive art and polished gameplay.

If anything, the oversaturation of the market with similar titles that are striving for the same level of commercial success has driven innovation in the market. Making games is a risky endeavor and if there are already x amount of minecraft clone cash-grabs then devs are being forced to innovate on the formulas in their own way. Imitation is the purest form of flattery. Remember when no one knew what a rogue-like (rogue-lite?? whatever it is) was besides the small niche community that played them? Now there is an explosion of those types of games. To be fair 98% are absolute garbage, but the 2% that succeed are amazing (Enter the Gungeon, Rogue Legacy, Darkest Dungeon etc.)

There are several titles in particular that are coming soon out of the indie scene that I am excited for, such as Pyre from Supermassive Games (creators of Bastion and Transistor). And from what I can tell, it is a far cry from any of their previous titles both thematically and gameplay-wise.

But it seems that no matter what games come out, the ones that are popular or that others try to imitate will always get shit for not being unique enough... Bullshit. These guys are the driving force in the creative scene and they do so in an incredibly competitive market. If a game is not your cup of tea there is no shortage of games from indie devs that break away from this "formula" and that are from any genre you can think of, albeit at varying levels of quality.

If anything, all the indie scene needs is better curation by distributors to weed out the shitty copycats while not giving unfair preference to the "bigger" indie devs.
